items.title: Greg Thomas interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: I had a recording of his in high school... And it had Clark, Clifford Brown and Maynard Ferguson playing together. So I mean I knew who he was.

ctx.x: That’s a powerful moment in playing beside the fellas from that generation is indescribable. It’s like this really intense education. And sometimes you don’t realize it until a little bit after when you reflect on what that was like.

Right. I mean it’s like truly living jazz history, you know? I mean he not only played with the greats — I mean I had a recording of his in high school and it was him, and it was a bootleg. It was a Dinah Washington recording. And it had Clark, Clifford Brown and Maynard Ferguson playing together. And it was just incredible. So I mean I knew who he was. So I’ll give you a quick anecdote. I was very close with Duke Ellington’s nephew, Ruth Ellington’s son, Michael James, who was one of the top protégés of Albert…

I recall being surprised I guess, early on when I started doing these interviews, when a person of Clark’s stature, a number of them would basically hit me up for a gig afterwards, after the interview. Now that sounds too pejorative. But it made me realize that these gentlemen, as much as they were revered by you and I and the jazz-loving public, were still trying to make a living.
